skill.name: developer-experience
skill.description: Guides developer environment setup, workflow automation, onboarding documentation, editor tooling, git hooks, and command shortcuts for software projects.
skill.summary: Improves project setup, developer workflows, tooling, and onboarding documentation.
skill.author: Joseph OBrien

security_audit.summary: The static findings are documentation examples, Markdown fences, or onboarding placeholders rather than executable malicious behavior. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or covert persistence intent was found in SKILL.md or references/onboarding-guide.template.md. The skill should still advise users to review environment and shell profile changes before applying generated setup guidance.

remediation.issue: Environment setup examples can be copied into real projects without review.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to inspect generated .env files and avoid committing secrets after copying templates.

remediation.issue: Optional shell profile alias examples mention ~/.zshrc and ~/.bashrc.
remediation.suggestion: Ask users to review, back up, and approve shell profile edits before applying aliases.

content.value_statement: Development setup often takes too long and leaves new contributors blocked. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code design setup guides, scripts, shortcuts, and tooling improvements.
actual_capabilities: Reviews project setup steps and identifies sources of developer friction.
Suggests setup scripts, package commands, Makefile tasks, and shell aliases.
Creates onboarding guide structure with prerequisites, access needs, and verification steps.
Recommends editor configuration, linting, formatting, and debug task improvements.
Designs git hook workflows for linting, tests, and commit quality checks.
Documents troubleshooting steps and success metrics for developer workflows.
limitations: Generated commands must be reviewed before they run on a real system.
The skill does not know private project policies unless they are provided.
It cannot guarantee every tool version or dependency is available locally.
Shell, git hook, and environment file changes may need team approval.

use_cases.title: Speed Up New Project Setup
use_cases.description: Create a clear setup path with prerequisites, install steps, environment templates, and verification checks.

use_cases.title: Improve Team Onboarding
use_cases.description: Build an onboarding guide that explains access, project structure, workflow expectations, and first-week tasks.

use_cases.title: Reduce Repeated Local Tasks
use_cases.description: Identify repeated commands and convert them into package scripts, Makefile tasks, editor tasks, or safe aliases.

prompt_templates.title: Review Setup Friction
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a project setup flow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this repository setup process. List the steps that may block a new developer and suggest clear improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Create Onboarding Guide
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an onboarding guide for this project with prerequisites, access needs, install steps, verification checks, and troubleshooting notes.

prompt_templates.title: Design Workflow Automation
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate automation planning for repeated development tasks.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze common development tasks in this project. Recommend package scripts, Makefile tasks, git hooks, and editor tasks with safety notes.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Developer Feedback Loops
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of build, test, lint, and local development speed.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the developer feedback loop for this repository. Prioritize changes that reduce setup time, test time, build time, and manual coordination.

output_examples.input: Review our setup process for a Node.js project.
output: A setup audit that identifies missing version checks, unclear environment steps, and manual dependency work.
A prioritized improvement list with setup validation, clearer documentation, and safer first-run commands.

output_examples.input: Create onboarding material for a new backend engineer.
output: A day-by-day onboarding outline covering access, local setup, project structure, test workflow, and troubleshooting.
A checklist that separates required access, optional tools, and first contribution tasks.

output_examples.input: Find ways to reduce repeated local commands.
output: A workflow plan that groups repeated tasks into package scripts, editor tasks, and project shortcuts.
Safety notes for commands that touch environment files, shell profiles, or generated build output.

best_practices: Review every generated command before running it in a local or shared environment.
Keep setup guidance project-specific, versioned, and tested by a new contributor.
Prefer reversible automation with clear verification steps and helpful error messages.
anti_patterns: Do not add shell profile changes without user approval and a backup plan.
Do not hide required access, secrets, or manual setup steps inside vague instructions.
Do not create automation that runs destructive cleanup commands without context.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps improve project setup, onboarding, local workflows, editor tooling, git hooks, and repeated development tasks.

faq.question: Can it write setup scripts?
faq.answer: Yes. It can propose setup scripts and commands, but users should review them before running anything.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it improve onboarding documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. It can structure onboarding guides with prerequisites, access needs, verification steps, and troubleshooting notes.

faq.question: Will it automatically change my shell profile?
faq.answer: No. It may suggest aliases, but profile changes should only happen after explicit user review and approval.

faq.question: What should teams provide for best results?
faq.answer: Provide the current README, package scripts, tool versions, common setup failures, and team workflow expectations.
